name: Purpose: to, in order to, so that
subtitle: Say why you do something with to + verb (I'm saving money to buy a car), in order to (a bit more formal) or so that + a new clause (I gave her my key so that she can water the plants).
source: icanspeak Spanish original English text (grammar-b1 run, 2026-10-29)

concept.exampleHtml: I'm saving money to buy a car. · I gave her my key so that she can water the plants.

qa.html: A purpose clause says why you do something. It answers Why? or What for? Why are you going to the bank? — To take out some money.

The same person does both things: use to + base verb. You don't say the subject again. I'm saving money to buy a car. In order to means the same, but it sounds a little more formal: I'm saving money in order to buy a car. For a negative purpose use in order not to or so as not to: We left early in order not to miss the train.

Another person acts in the purpose? Then use so that + subject + verb. The verb is often can (now) or could (past): I gave Tom my key so that he can water the plants. She spoke slowly so that we could understand.
for goes before a noun, never before a verb. I went to the shop for some bread. It means the same as I went to the shop to buy some bread.

Typical mistakes: ✗ I went to the shop for to buy bread. / …for buy bread. → ✓ I went to the shop to buy bread. (or: for bread) · ✗ I gave Tom my key to he water the plants. → ✓ …so that he can water the plants. · ✗ I'm saving money so that to buy a car. → ✓ …to buy a car.

concept.noteHtml: So that starts a clause with its own subject and verb. When the same person acts, to is shorter and more natural, but so that I can is also correct: I got up early so that I could catch the bus. You don't need want or will in a to clause: say I'm saving money to buy a car, not to want to buy. For more about to + verb, see -ing or to. For can and could, see Modal verbs.

items: in order to = to, but more formal: I'm saving money in order to buy a car.
Negative: in order not to / so as not to: I set two alarms in order not to oversleep.
Now or future: so that + can: I'm speaking slowly so that you can understand.
Past: so that + could: She spoke slowly so that we could understand.
What do you need the key for? — To open the cellar.
Why are you buying flowers? — So that my mum feels better.
The short answer is only the purpose clause.
Why? can ask for a reason or a purpose. What … for? asks for the purpose.

listen.text: I'm going to the bank to take out some money.
listen.note: Same person: to + base verb. The subject is not repeated.

listen.text: I gave my neighbour a key so that she can water the plants.
listen.note: Another person acts: so that + her own subject and verb. Can is very common.

listen.text: What do you need the form for? To apply for a passport.
listen.note: Ask Why? or What … for? The short answer is only the purpose.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose what you hear: to, so that or in order to? Think about who acts.

items.text: I'm learning English to work in a hospital.
choices: so that she works in a hospital

items.text: We're talking quietly so that the baby can sleep.
choices: so that the baby can sleep

items.text: I left early so that I could catch the bus.
choices: so that I can catch the bus
so that I could catch the bus

items.text: The teacher repeats the rule so that everyone understands.
In order to save money, we cook at home.
What do you need my address for?
choices: What do you need my address for
Why do you need my address
Where do you need my address

rounds.label: 1 · to + verb
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences about the same person. Join them with to. Leave out want.

example.prompt: I'm going to the bank. I want to take out some money.
example.answer: I'm going to the bank to take out some money.

items.prompt: I'm going to the doctor. I want to get a prescription.
items.answer: I'm going to the doctor to get a prescription.

items.prompt: We're saving money. We want to travel in summer.
items.answer: We're saving money to travel in summer.

items.prompt: She's doing a course. She wants to become an accountant.
items.answer: She's doing a course to become an accountant.

items.prompt: I'm phoning the office. I want to make an appointment.
items.answer: I'm phoning the office to make an appointment.

items.prompt: He's going into town. He wants to buy a suit.
items.answer: He's going into town to buy a suit.

items.prompt: We're getting up early. We want to catch the first train.
items.answer: We're getting up early to catch the first train.

rounds.label: 2 · so that: another person
rounds.instruction: You hear two sentences. In the second, another person acts. Join them with so that and can.

example.prompt: I'm leaving you the key. You should lock the door.
example.answer: I'm leaving you the key so that you can lock the door.

items.prompt: I'm writing to the landlord. He should fix the heating.
items.answer: I'm writing to the landlord so that he can fix the heating.

items.prompt: I'm cooking early today. The children should eat on time.
items.answer: I'm cooking early today so that the children can eat on time.

items.prompt: I'm switching on the light. The guests should find the door.
items.answer: I'm switching on the light so that the guests can find the door.

items.prompt: I'm giving my daughter some money. She should buy bread.
items.answer: I'm giving my daughter some money so that she can buy bread.

items.prompt: Amira is lending Tom her bike. He should get to work on time.
items.answer: Amira is lending Tom her bike so that he can get to work on time.

items.prompt: We're speaking slowly. The new colleague should understand everything.
items.answer: We're speaking slowly so that the new colleague can understand everything.

exercises.title: to or so that? Complete the sentences.
exercises.hint: Look at what follows the gap. A base verb and no new subject: to. A new subject and a verb: so that.
exercises.hintHtml: toNo new subject: to + base verb.so thatA new subject and a verb: so that + clause.

items.prompt: I'm going to the bank ___ take out some money.
items.why: No new subject, and a base verb follows: to take.

items.prompt: I gave my neighbour a key ___ she can water the plants.
items.why: A new subject (she) and a verb (can water): so that.

items.prompt: We're talking quietly ___ the baby can sleep.
items.why: The baby is a new subject, so use so that.

items.prompt: Olga is doing a course ___ get a better job.
items.why: Olga does both things. A base verb follows: to get.

items.prompt: The doctor wrote me a prescription ___ I could get the tablets.
items.why: The clause has its own subject (I) and could: so that.

items.prompt: I set two alarms ___ I don't oversleep.
items.why: A clause with its own subject and verb (I don't oversleep) needs so that.

items.prompt: The parents work hard ___ their children can study.
items.why: The children are a new subject: so that.

items.prompt: ___ save money, we often shop in the sales.
items.why: No new subject, and a base verb follows: To save money.

exercises.title: The same person or another one?
exercises.hint: Who acts in the second sentence? The same person: both patterns work (to or so that). Another person: only so that.

rows.term: I'm saving money. I want to buy a car.
I'm saving money. My daughter should go to university.
We're leaving early. We don't want to miss the train.
I'm writing to the landlord. He should repair the heating.
Tom is cooking. The children should have something hot to eat.
Olga is phoning the clinic. She wants to make an appointment.
The teacher explains the task again. Everyone should understand it.
I'm going to the bank. I want to open an account.

exercises.title: Complete the purpose.
exercises.hint: to + base verb. so that + subject + can / could. for + noun, never for + verb.

items.prompt: I'm writing down her number to ___ her later. (call)
items.why: After to, use the base verb: to call.

items.prompt: I'm giving you my number so that you ___ me. (call)
items.why: After so that, use a subject and a verb: you can call.

items.prompt: She spoke slowly so that we ___ everything. (understand)
items.why: The story is in the past, so use could: we could understand.

items.prompt: We're hiring a van so that our friends ___ the sofa. (carry)
items.why: Our friends are a new subject: so that + can carry.

items.prompt: We left early in order ___ the train. (not / miss)
items.why: The negative is in order not to + base verb.

items.prompt: I wake my son twice so that he ___ the bus. (not / miss)
items.why: He is a new subject: so that he doesn't miss.

items.prompt: I went to the shop ___ some milk.
items.why: A noun follows (some milk): use for.

items.prompt: I went to the shop ___ buy some milk.
items.why: A verb follows (buy): use to. Never for to.

exercises.title: Match the purpose.
exercises.hint: Tap the first part of a sentence, then the purpose that fits.
